verdict.line: You lose when Rupture's zone or Feral Scream's cone catches you standing still near his Feast range; you win by dodging both zones outright and out-scaling him once your core items land.

brief.thesis: Cho'Gath's whole kit is area-based — Rupture (Q) hits a ground zone, Feral Scream (W) hits a cone, Vorpal Spikes cleave everyone in front of him — none of it 'targets' you directly, so Hallowed Mist (W) barely helps, since it only blocks enemies who try to target you specifically. That gap is the real reason this sits at a 43.8% win rate over 137 games despite an 'even' lane shape: Gwen's one defensive tool doesn't defang this specific kit, which is why the data hands Cho the solo-kill edge and calls the matchup defensive.

theirWindow.when: Rupture and Feral Scream both up
theirWindow.what: He can knock you up with Rupture, silence your E and Flash with Feral Scream, and go for Feast (R, 175 range) once you're low — treat this combo as lethal and disengage before he strings it.

yourWindow.when: Rupture and Feral Scream both on cooldown
yourWindow.what: He has nothing but autos and Vorpal Spikes for roughly the next several seconds — dash in with Skip 'n Slash (E) and stack Snip Snip! (Q) procs for the free trade.

powerCurve.note: Feral Scream silence shuts down E combos
Feast threatens kills, grants permanent stacks
Shorter E cooldown lets you trade back

start.why: 92% pick rate and the highest sample win rate (47.2% over 161 games) — the extra sustain matters against Rupture/Vorpal Spikes poke you can't fully dodge.

boots.why: Highest measured win rate on boots (54.3% over 70 games) — you need the magic penetration to shorten trades before Feral Scream or Feast punishes you for standing still.

core.why: First item in the best-performing build path (60% win rate over 35 games).
Second item in that same path — the burst amp matters since you can't out-sustain him through Carnivore healing.
Completes the 60%-win-rate core — by this point you're past the level 6-8 danger window and scaling into your favoured levels.

situational.when: the game goes long and you need sustain damage to outlast his stacked health from Feast kills
you want faster Snip Snip! (Q) cycling to stack A Thousand Cuts procs in extended trades

runes.keystoneWhy: Stacks through the short trades you're forced into around his cooldowns, and converts to healing — useful since your W doesn't stop his AOE damage.

summoners.why: The 51% win-rate, 59.2%-pick combo — Ignite punishes the short trade windows you get when his Q/W are down, since you won't out-sustain Carnivore's healing on even trades.

playing.title: Don't rely on mist to dodge zones
playing.detail: Hallowed Mist (W) only stops enemies who target you directly — Rupture's ground zone and Feral Scream's cone still hit you if you're standing in them. Reposition physically, don't trust the shield.

playing.title: Trade only after Feral Scream is down
playing.detail: Feral Scream (W, 13s CD, 300 range cone) silences you for a few seconds, locking out E and Flash. Bait it onto a minion wave, then dash in with Skip 'n Slash while it's on cooldown.

playing.title: Respect Feast below 30% HP
playing.detail: Feast (R, 60s CD, 175 range) deals high true damage and permanently grows him if it kills you. Disengage before it's off cooldown if you're under roughly 30% health from level 6 onward.

playing.title: Stack Q procs in every trade
playing.detail: Snip Snip! deals true damage in its center hits and applies A Thousand Cuts, healing you off champion damage. Land multiple snips per trade rather than one poke and retreat.

playing.title: Reset with E, don't greed it
playing.detail: Skip 'n Slash refunds its cooldown if you hit an enemy during the empowered window. Land it, take the attack speed window, then leave — don't stay in Vorpal Spikes range for a second combo.

playing.title: Play passive through level 8
playing.detail: Solo-kill risk favors him until Feast's threat window passes and your core items land. Farm through poke rather than forcing all-ins before level 9.

playing.title: Look for kills from level 9 on
playing.detail: Once Skip 'n Slash is rank 3+ and Shadowflame is online, your burst and sustain both outscale his flat true damage threats — this is where you flip the lane.

brief.patchCaveat: Build, runes, summoners, and all win rates/sample sizes above are measured from live games on the current patch via OP.GG; the mechanical reasoning — why mist doesn't help here, the Feast/Rupture/Feral Scream timing windows — is my own tactical read, not measured data.
